items.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010
items.q: My husband, Rick Montalbano, helps out a lot with the tour managing... We’re a team.

ctx.x: Well thank you for leading into my next question. What do you think singers should be able to convey to their band?

Everything. Unless you want to have a musical director who you need to be able to communicate clearly with, and a lot of singers choose to do that. I mean I don’t have a musical director but my pianist, Michael, he does a lot of the arrangements, he holds on to all the charts for us, my bass player, I should say Michael Kanan. Neil Miner, my bass player, does a lot of arrangements too. My husband, Rick Montalbano, helps out a lot with the tour managing and just doing all the day-to-day business with our…
Well how much of that did you learn at the Manhattan School of Music?

items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: play with my son and my daughter-in-law [Jane Monheit]

ctx.x: Well here’s a hard one to sort of wrap up here. Do you remember, is there any gig or a series of gigs stand out as one of the most memorable or greatest things ever?

Hmm. That’s a tough question. I don’t know, Monk. I don’t think I could pick a particular gig. I could tell you some of the things I’ve really gotten a lot of enjoyment out of lately, when I get to the chance to play with my son and my daughter-in-law [Jane Monheit], in that setting, when their piano player — a couple of weeks ago he was in Spain I guess doing something and they had a gig in Massachusetts so I went in and filled in and it was just a ball to play in that setting with them, and to play with my son,…

without that gig. You know it’s one of those opportunities to do original material and arrangements, organized. You know we’ve played together so long. And it’s a little odd combination of things so the way we voice things and work out arrangements is a source of interest. J.R. Monterose used to say “you’ve got to stay interested.” When he first started saying it — but the older I get I realize that’s so true. That’s so true. I look for things that interest me. Musical opportunities.
